newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE white sugar edges lower but NY stays focus.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE white sugar edges lower but NY stays focus.

text.p: White sugar futures were content to hover around intraday lows in thin volume on Tuesday as the New York market took centre stage before the May raws expiry, traders said.
Outright selling by some trade players, coupled with some against actuals interest, caused the August/October spread to narrow further to under $8.00 nominal value.
Nearby August dominated the light overall volume of 643 lots, down 80 cents at $312.30 at 1520 GMT. October was down 30 cents at $304.50.
Technical analysts said August would be well supported at between $307 and $309 by its recent uptrend and short-term moving averages.
Traders said the August/July white/raw differential would attract selling interest at $70 and above, while buyers would stay away unless it narrowed to around $64.

New York was the real focus of attention given that the May contract expires on April 30 and speculators are still holding long positions, they said. July raws dipped under 11.00 cents/lb but failed to trigger sell-stops.
In Paris nearby positions also moved lower but volume was very thin at just 215 lots.
August was down $1.00 at $312.30 and October down 80 cents at $314.20.
Physical news on the whites remained thin on the ground but there was more of interest on the raws.
Egypt is reported to have agreed to resell some of its Brazilian raw sugar contracts because of a surplus.
Egyptian companies contracted to buy about 500,000 tonnes of raws and some deliveries will be deferred to March 1998 from July 1997.
The International Sugar Organization (ISO) said Russia was once again the largest country of destination for Cuban sugar in 1996, more than doubling its imports compared with 1995
Russia imported 1.83 million tonnes of Cuban raws last year after 722,051 in 1995, the ISO said.
